recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If a future work group decision wants the Shareable/Publishable/Authoring repository capability statements copied or re-owned by FHIR core, handle that as a new substantive change coordinated with CRMI.
issue_request: FHIR-32643 was an Applied/Persuasive CDS issue asking FHIR core to consider knowledge artifact repository capability statements, initially by generalizing QM IG measure repository service capability statements into ShareableArtifactRepository, PublishableArtifactRepository, and AuthoringArtifactRepository capabilities. Later Jira comments narrowed the applied core action to adding discussion of these capabilities and referencing CRMI for the formal capability statements.
initial_application: The issue was applied by commit 0b4226bcd1f7ab7f5b2b8c5f0b6cfd32a59a97a5 in merged PR HL7/fhir#3369, which added CRMI Artifact Repository Service and Artifact Terminology Service links to source/clinicalreasoning-knowledge-artifact-distribution.html. No separate core commit added the three formal CRMI capability statements to FHIR core, matching the later Jira direction that formal statements live in CRMI.
additional_context: The Clinical Reasoning module links to the Sharing Knowledge Artifacts page and lists a minimum Knowledge Repository service while indicating that more detailed treatment is available in CRMI and the Quality Measure IG. The CRMI Artifact Repository Service page currently documents the formal ShareableArtifactRepository, PublishableArtifactRepository, and AuthoringArtifactRepository capability statements. Later Applied issue FHIR-53084 updated the same artifact distribution topic to informative/recommendation wording but preserved the CRMI links added for FHIR-32643.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current build-scoped source already provides the core discussion and CRMI references requested by the applied Jira comments, and copying the CRMI formal capability statements into core would duplicate content now owned by CRMI.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied clarification on the same Clinical Reasoning artifact distribution topic changed the page to informative and reworded recommendations while preserving the CRMI capability links.
